reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Arbitrum liquidity pools as expected to generate more than 200% within days and demonstrates cryptocurrency deposits and smart-contract approvals. It also presents a 25% annualized return without risk of loss, linking unusually high-return claims to financial participation. The records do not establish that any return occurred or that the claim was guaranteed, and the separate Prime XBT referral is not established as connected to the demonstrated strategy.

opening.argument: Judge, read the return figures as investment commentary, not a promise. The speaker says he lacks absolute confidence about where the market may go, acknowledges that higher-APR searches leave fewer options, and says he does not know whether a project's stated capacity goal will be filled. He also adjusts the size of one proposed pool because a price move could cause a loss. Those qualifications matter when interpreting his later optimism: he is weighing uncertain opportunities and describing a position he intends to manage, not establishing that any viewer will earn the quoted rate.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest line says the pools will generate more than 200%, but the sentence itself begins with “in principle”; it reports an expectation, not a completed return. The 25% figure is likewise framed as something that “would be brutal,” not a result the speaker says he achieved. Contract approval shows how a position is entered; it does not, by itself, prove that a promised payout exists.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the actionable pitch. After walking through deposits and approvals, the speaker tells viewers the two pools “will be generating more than 200% in the next few days.” He also invokes a return “without risk of loss.” Neither statement is supported by an observed payout in the supplied material, yet both are tied to participation in investment pools.

opening.argument: Judge, the video is an operational walkthrough of the speaker's own DeFi allocation. He introduces it as a decision about his Orca pool and a step-by-step account of new investments. He then explains how to filter positions, transfer his assets to Arbitrum, choose price ranges, and calculate the tokens needed for a deposit. The detailed sequence is consistent with demonstrating how he constructs and manages a position. Even the discussion of high APRs is presented as a search filter, not evidence that a viewer has received or will receive that return.

we're going to have to do the calculations to know how much UMAMI and how much RAP Ethereum we're going to have to deposit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution accurately identifies deposits and approvals, but those are also the ordinary steps a walkthrough must explain. Its quotation about 200% is a forward-looking statement made after the speaker says the positions are set up; it does not document a payout. The separate staking discussion describes proposed ways to generate income, not a staking deposit demonstrated in the cited Uniswap sequence.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still promote the investment it teaches. Here the speaker says viewers will see strategies replicated, demonstrates contract approval and liquidity deposits, then predicts the resulting pools will generate more than 200% within days. The tutorial framing does not remove the high-return inducement attached to those steps.

opening.argument: Judge, the visible mechanism is the speaker using named trading and liquidity interfaces for his own transactions, not directing funds to an account he controls. He describes converting assets on Kucoin, choosing an Arbitrum withdrawal, and adding liquidity through Uniswap; the closing description separately carries a Prime XBT registration link and promotional code. The record does not connect that referral to the demonstrated pools, show a credential request from viewers, or establish that viewers must pay the speaker to participate. The return estimates deserve scrutiny, but they do not establish an operator-run collection scheme in this record.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's evidence supports a concerning return claim and a deposit walkthrough, but not that deposits go to the speaker or that the Prime XBT referral funds the pools. Its own account leaves that connection unestablished. A MetaMask approval and liquidity transaction identify participation in the described pool; they do not establish a separate payment demand or credential-harvesting step.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on proving that the speaker personally receives deposits or that the separate referral is connected. He directs attention to pools selected for 100% to 300% APR, shows how to approve and add funds, and then says the resulting pools will generate more than 200% in the next few days. The missing payment-to-speaker mechanism does not answer that investment-return promotion.
